name: Kulhus
description:
In May 1908 Hakon Høeg Jarner, the geologist of the Danmark Expedition, discovered an open deposit of coal on the east side of Peters Bugt on Hochstetter Forland. The place was named "Jarners Kulmine" (coal mine). Later on the good "Hochstetter coal" was used in many of the stoves on the coast and on several expedition vessels.

The presence of the coal was also the direct reason that Lauge Koch decided to build one of his expedition houses at this place: "In 1932 the station Kulhus was erected on Hochstetter Forland. It was built there, because the surface of the ground was strewn with coal fragments, so sufficient coal to heat the house could be picked up in the immediate neighbourhood of the station. In the bay the coal leading layers are clearly visible. Further south along the 250 m high mountain "Negeren", the coal leading layeres are even more distinctive."

Originally Kulhus was just meant to be a travellers station, but during the winter 1932-33 four members of the Three-Year Expedition wintered here. Kulhus was also used for wintering in 1934-35 by trappers.

In 2022-23 Kulhus was restored by NANOK.

The house must always be left only in a good condition, meaning:

  • All doors and windows / shutters securely closed
  • Coal stove cleaned for ashes and ready for use
  • Coal bucket filled with coal
  • Pieces of firewood put in paraffin
  • Matchboxes with matches ready in opening
  • House nicely swept and cleaned all over
  • No food or garbage left behind
  • No equipment or provisions left behind. Such equipment or provisions will be removed by NANOK without prior notice at the owners expense.

Aage V. Jensens Fonde sponsor Nanok's work.

Number in brackets [ ] refer to hut number in Peter Schmidt Mikkelsen: "North-East Greenland 1908-60.  The Trapper Era"  (2008) published by Scott Polar Research Institute.
